selection_reason: No completed experiments provide evidence, so the priority is to establish a simple, low-risk baseline and reduce uncertainty about whether basic RNA profiling alone is informative. config_001 tests a minimal RNA-only single-profile model with a standard PCA representation, clarifying the reference performance of the RNA branch before adding complexity. It is the best first experiment under a limited budget because it is simple, interpretable, and provides an anchor for later comparisons of multiprofile aggregation, learned RNA encoders, image modality, and multimodal fusion.

Only the RNA PCA single-profile baseline is known (0.485 accuracy, 0.464 F1), leaving image modality completely untested. config_010 tests whether image alone with a simple ResNet50 single-profile model provides competitive signal, isolating the modality effect without adding aggregation or fusion. This is the highest-value next step because it establishes a second unimodal baseline and clarifies whether future budget should prioritize image, RNA, or multimodal fusion.

RNA-only PCA singleprofile is much stronger than image-only ResNet (acc 0.485/F1 0.464 vs 0.208/0.172), so the next step should exploit the RNA direction while testing a key remaining design choice: whether multiple profiles with simple aggregation help. config_002 keeps the same RNA encoder and model type but changes to multiprofile with avgpool, isolating the profile/aggregation effect before trying transformer aggregation, learned encoders, or multimodal fusion. This is a simple, high-value experiment under a limited budget.

The strongest evidence so far is that multiprofile RNA with PCA and avgpool (config_002) substantially improves over single-profile RNA PCA (config_001), suggesting profile aggregation is important. The main remaining uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation can further improve over avgpool under the same RNA encoder and profile setting. config_003 isolates this by changing only aggregation from avgpool to transformer, making it the most efficient next test to exploit the promising multiprofile RNA direction without confounding encoder or modality changes.

The strongest completed result is RNA-only multiprofile with avgpool and PCA, with validation accuracy 0.591 and F1 0.573, clearly better than single-profile PCA and transformer aggregation. The key remaining uncertainty is whether a learned RNA representation can improve on PCA in this already promising profile/aggregation setting. config_005 changes only the RNA encoder to scvi_n200 while keeping RNA-only, multiprofile, and avgpool fixed, so it isolates the representation effect. This is a focused exploitation of the best current direction with higher expected accuracy than image-only, and it will clarify whether future multimodal experiments should be built on PCA or a learned RNA embedding.

The strongest evidence so far is RNA-only multiprofile with avgpool, especially scvi_n200, which reached 0.650 accuracy and 0.628 F1, clearly above PCA multiprofile avgpool at 0.591/0.573. Aggregation also appears important, since avgpool beat transformer for PCA. The main remaining uncertainty is whether another learned RNA representation, scgpt, can match or exceed scvi under the same favorable profile and aggregation settings. config_008 changes only the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 to scgpt while keeping multiprofile and avgpool, so it isolates the representation effect. This is the best next use of budget because it exploits the current best profile/aggregation setting, tests an unexplored important design choice, and avoids premature multimodal fusion before the best unimodal representation is established.

Completed runs show RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200 with avgpool is the clear best unimodal setting, with 0.650 accuracy and 0.628 F1, while image-only ResNet50 is weak at 0.208 accuracy. This leaves important uncertainty about whether image features can add value when fused with the strongest RNA representation. config_030 keeps the best RNA settings fixed and adds only a ResNet50 image branch with simple concat fusion, so it directly tests the effect of adding image/fusion relative to the best unimodal baseline. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the strongest existing direction while minimally exploring the central multimodal/fusion question; if it improves, it identifies a promising multimodal path, and if it does not, it discourages more complex multimodal variants.

The strongest evidence is that RNA-only scvi_n200 with multiprofile avgpool is best (acc 0.650, F1 0.628), while the only multimodal extension with ResNet50 and concat is slightly weaker (acc 0.632, F1 0.607); image-only ResNet50 is also weak, so the key uncertainty is whether the lack of multimodal gain is due to a weak image encoder. config_036 tests exactly this by replacing ResNet50 with imagenet_vit_l while keeping scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool, and concat fixed, isolating image representation. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the best RNA pipeline, directly clarifies whether a stronger image modality can make the model competitive, and avoids changing multiple factors at once.

The strongest result so far is config_036, where multimodal scvi + ViT + avgpool reaches 0.715 accuracy, while the same RNA backbone with ResNet multimodal fusion did not beat RNA-only. This suggests the ViT image encoder may be driving the gain, but image-only ViT performance is still unknown. config_014 tests image-only ViT with the same multiprofile/avgpool setting, clarifying whether the improvement comes from the image representation itself or from fusion with RNA. This is a high-value ablation of the current best direction and reduces uncertainty about modality contribution before further exploiting fusion or aggregation choices.

The strongest completed result is config_036 (scvi RNA, ViT-L image, multiprofile avgpool, concat) with validation accuracy 0.715, clearly above the best RNA-only model and suggesting that the ViT image branch adds useful information. The main remaining uncertainty for this promising multimodal setup is whether the fusion rule matters: only concat has been tested for this exact representation/profile/aggregation combination. config_037 changes only the fusion from concat to weighted, cleanly isolating the fusion effect while preserving the current best design. This is the best next experiment because it both exploits the strongest evidence and tests whether a simple fusion improvement can further increase validation accuracy under a limited budget.
